details:
Q1: How should an `ai:priority` label on the linked issue give the PR priority in the merge-lease queue? Today the lease queue only looks at labels on the PR itself.
Choices:
A) Extend the lease ordering so a PR whose verified linked issue carries a `MERGE_TRAIN_PRIORITY_LABELS` label also ranks in the priority group. It uses the same checks as `_mt_pr_is_priority`: head `${MT_PREFIX}<M>`, `headRefName` match, `M` in `closingIssuesReferences`, same-repository head. It reuses the linked-issue labels the merge train already reads, with no new per-PR read in a loop. If those labels can't be read, the PR gets no priority. Ranking by the PR's own labels and by `MERGE_LEASE_PRIORITY_HEAD_PREFIXES` stays as it is. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Leave the lease ordering as it is, and have the pipeline copy `ai:priority` from the verified linked issue onto the PR, so the existing PR-label check ranks it. This adds label writes and a PR label that can drift out of sync with the issue.
C) Take lease priority out of scope. `ai:priority` only affects the merge train, review and final-CI ordering, and the pressure hold. Implementation step 4 is replaced by a test showing the lease ordering is unchanged.
